FINDINGS.finding: The one-use retry authority has a real reauthorization window. retry_authorized rejects an existing retry only when m["retry"] exists and used is false. After claim_retry appends retry_started, used becomes true while the next attempt has not yet been attempt_bound. During that interval authorize_retry for the same failed attempt passes again, replaces m["retry"] with a fresh authorization_id and can yield the same next attempt a second time. That violates the PLAN requirement that claim_retry be one-use across restore/crash boundaries and creates a path to duplicate explicit retry directives.

The existing retry test proves that the same authorization token is not regranted after claim/restore, but it does not attempt to create a new retry_authorized event after retry_started and before the claimed next attempt is bound. Therefore the current 189-pass suite does not cover the exact duplicate-retry window above.

The rest of the core retry flow is directionally correct: authorization requires the latest bound attempt to be failed/uncertain; retry_started is appended before returning the directive; the directive preserves profile/mission/request/control/original_expected_commit and advances attempt_id; completed replies or receipts block retry; and actual transmission remains outside the registry behind existing Fresh /retry authority.

Immutable review identity is otherwise handled correctly. mission_started freezes original_expected_commit, checkpoint_recorded advances only checkpoint_head, recovery validates the current workspace against the audited checkpoint, and current HEAD is not substituted into reply/retry identity.

The registry implements the major durability/isolation requirements: exactly two immutable profiles, distinct canonical paths/branches, same authorized repository and credential-free allowed remote forms, one globally active mission, global request/control collision checks, sequential attempt binding, duplicate target rejection, deterministic hash-chained events/sealed head, OS single-writer locking and replay-only restore with no Git/Chrome/send callback.

The bounded two-worktree evidence is coherent. integration/result.json reports two profiles, original commits for A and B, B later checkpoint 73b31983a5635943984d78ede7187b1074ad41e8, original_commit_preserved=true, cross_profile_reply_rejected=true, one_use_retry_permission=true and implicit_restore_operations=0. The B checkpoint commit was independently fetched: it is one commit after 94048305c8cb9cfd6c8abb003bc601ff25fcf90d and adds only executed_scope.json, so the GitHub evidence supports the original-commit-preservation claim. That integration success does not eliminate the synthetic registry reauthorization defect because the problematic second-authorization interleaving was not exercised.

All five independently fetched blobs listed in m3/draft/source_hashes.json match their declared Git blob IDs. The implementation commit 94e0091cfbe4b6248f388c620b397ab2ba733b1e is one bounded commit after the M3 PLAN authority, and incoming 799641d11071a04b1452ba6a6c8ddb3ce69e61a9 is one evidence-only commit after the implementation. Reported gates are 189 Python passes, 181 Node passes, 27 syntax files, manifest PASS and diff PASS.

REVIEW_SUMMARY: The exact incoming authority 799641d11071a04b1452ba6a6c8ddb3ce69e61a9 and every required incoming path/ref were independently read through the official GitHub connector. The M3 draft substantially implements the two-profile workspace authority, immutable-original-commit model, sealed audit state, single-writer locking, safe restore and bounded Chrome integration requested by the PLAN. However, one concrete retry-state defect remains: after a one-use retry has been claimed but before its next attempt is bound, a second retry_authorized event for the same failed attempt can replace the used authorization and yield the same next attempt again. This directly violates the mission's one-use explicit-retry invariant and is not covered by the current tests. CHANGES_REQUIRED is therefore necessary for one bounded state-machine correction plus focused regression, after which the corrected candidate should return for final independent M3 review.
